routes.label: Square the pension relationships and eliminate

question: A retiring employee receives an annual pension proportional to the square root of the number of years of his service. Had he served \(a\) years more, his pension would have been \(p\) dollars greater, whereas, had he served \(b\) years more (\(b\ne a\)), his pension would have been \(q\) dollars greater than the original annual pension. Find his annual pension in terms of \(a,\) \(b,\) \(p,\) and \(q.\)
solution:
Use the contextual conditions \(a,b,p,q>0\), with the data compatible with the stated pension rule. Let \(t\geq0\) be the original years of service, let \(P\) be the original annual pension, and let \(k>0\) be the proportionality constant. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
P&=k\sqrt t,\\
P+p&=k\sqrt{t+a},\\
P+q&=k\sqrt{t+b}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Squaring is useful because it turns the extra years of service into simple differences. All the pension amounts are nonnegative, so there is no sign ambiguity. Subtracting \(P^2=k^2t\) from the other two squared equations gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2Pp+p^2&=ak^2,\\
2Pq+q^2&=bk^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiply the first equation by \(b\) and the second by \(a\), then subtract to eliminate \(k^2\):
\[
2P(bp-aq)=aq^2-bp^2.
\]
Before dividing, we must check that \(bp-aq\neq0\). If \(bp=aq\), this last equation also gives \(aq^2=bp^2\). Substituting \(bp=aq\) yields \(aq(q-p)=0\). Positivity forces \(q=p\), and then \(bp=aq\) forces \(b=a\), contrary to the hypothesis.

Therefore the annual pension is
\[
\boxed{P=\frac{aq^2-bp^2}{2(bp-aq)}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

The reduction and back-substitution leave one-variable linear equations that must be solved; this is not a claim that every route must name transposition.
The source expressly permits an area interpretation of the perfect-square identity; polynomial multiplication is one derivation, not the only route to the stated formula-use criteria.

Contrasting the independent identities usefully prevents confusing a square of a sum with a product of a sum and difference. No learning order is necessary, but that misconception-prevention role supports preparation rather than mere thematic association.
